title: wtm run config
description: Schema for .wtm/run.toml — declares jobs (services and tasks) and profiles that compose them.

port_offset_block.description: Spacing between two worktrees' ports. Each worktree holds an ordinal (0 for the main checkout) and every declared base port is shifted by ordinal x this block. Two base ports must not differ by a multiple of it: 3000 and 3010 with a block of 10 collide on the second worktree, while 5434/5435/5436 never do. Defaults to 10.

job.description: List of jobs the project can run.

name.description: Job name. Must be unique across all [[job]] entries in this file (enforced at load time). Referenced from profiles and from `wtm run start|stop|logs`.

kind.description: service = long-running process (pnpm dev, docker compose). task = one-shot script (pnpm migrate, pnpm seed) that must exit 0 before the profile continues.

cmd.description: Command to start the job, run as a `/bin/sh` line: quotes, `&&`, pipes, redirections and globs all mean what they mean in a terminal, and `${VAR}` expands from the job's environment — including the ports declared below. Write `pnpm dev --port ${PORT}` for a server that only takes its port as a CLI flag.

stop.description: Optional stop command. When set on a service, marks it as detached: wtm waits for `cmd` to exit on start (e.g. `docker compose up -d`) and uses `stop` to shut it down later. A `/bin/sh` line like `cmd`, run with the same environment and the same resolved ports. Tasks cannot have a stop command.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the worktree root. Defaults to the worktree root.

ports.description: Base ports this job binds, as ENV_VAR = port. wtm injects ENV_VAR = port + WTM_PORT_OFFSET, so the main checkout keeps the declared port and every other worktree gets a free one. Write the command to read the variable (PORT for a dev server) or template it into docker-compose ("${DB_PORT:-5432}:5432", the default keeping the file usable without wtm).

url.description: Publishes one of this job's declared ports under a name, so the worktree gets its own hostname instead of a port to remember — and its own cookie jar, since cookies ignore the port. Omit for a job that does not speak HTTP.

port.description: Name of the port to publish. Must be one of the keys declared in `ports` above — the name, not the number: the number depends on the worktree.

host.description: Host segment this job is published under, defaulting to the job's name. May contain dots to create an intermediate level: `web.app-1` puts the job under `.app-1.<worktree>.<project>.localhost`, which the app's siblings then share a cookie parent with.

probe.description: Whether `wtm run up` checks that this job's declared ports were actually bound. Set to false to stop reporting a service that binds the base port because its command never reads the injected variable — the fix is to pass --port ${PORT} to it, and this key acknowledges the warning until then. Omitted means true.

binds_no_port.description: Whether this service listens on nothing by design — a build in watch mode, a worker, or a runner whose children hold the ports. Silence reads as an oversight, so `wtm run init` keeps offering a port and the report keeps naming the job; this key answers the question once. A job declaring ports must not set it.

runs.description: The declared jobs this one starts itself — a `turbo run dev` against a filter, any single process that fans out. wtm infers nothing from the command: the relation is declared here. It gives the runner its children's urls, lets the port check look at their ports, and lets wtm refuse to start a runner alongside one of its own children.

scope.description: Set to "shared" to run this job ONCE for the whole repository instead of once per worktree — a postgres, a keycloak. It runs in the main checkout, so it takes no port offset (a declared 5432 is the 5432 it binds everywhere) and its published URL carries no worktree segment. Other worktrees hold a claim on it, reported as status "attached" with pid 0; the service stops when the last claim goes. Omit for the default, one instance per worktree.

tenant.description: The slice of a shared service this worktree gets, so each keeps its own data — a database, a set of keycloak realms. Only valid on a job with scope = "shared"; a shared job without one means one instance with one set of data. wtm names the tenant and runs the commands below, and knows nothing else about them.

name.description: The tenant's name. {worktree} and {ordinal} are substituted; the resolved value reaches the commands as $WTM_TENANT. e.g. "app_{worktree}".

attach.description: Command run the first time a worktree claims the service, to carve its tenant out — e.g. a CREATE DATABASE. Runs as a /bin/sh line with the worktree's whole environment (its ports and URLs) plus $WTM_TENANT, $WTM_WORKTREE and $WTM_ORDINAL. Retried for a while: the service was started moments earlier and may not be accepting connections yet.

detach.description: Command run by `wtm clean` when the worktree goes, to give the tenant back — e.g. a DROP DATABASE. Never run by `run stop` or `run down`: stopping is not destroying. `wtm clean --keep-data` withholds it. Same environment as attach.

env.description: Variables the tenant contributes, with {worktree} and {ordinal} substituted — e.g. CRM_DATABASE_URL = "postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/crm_{worktree}". They reach the attach and detach commands.

then.description: Tasks cannot declare a stop command.

profile.description: Named groups of jobs run together via `wtm run up [profile]`.

name.description: Profile name. Must be unique across all [[profile]] entries in this file (enforced at load time). Used as the argument to `wtm run up <name>`.

jobs.description: Ordered list of job names. Jobs run sequentially: tasks block, services start in the background. The same job cannot appear twice.

default.description: If true, this profile runs when `wtm run up` is invoked without a profile argument. At most one profile in the file can have default = true (enforced at load time).

env_port.description: Links a .env key to a declared port. wtm rewrites the port inside that key's value for each worktree, leaving the rest of the value untouched — so a hard-coded host:port in a URL follows the worktree's offset.

file.description: The .env target holding the key, as configured under [env] in .wtm.toml (e.g. ".env", "apps/web/.env").

key.description: The .env key whose value carries the port.

job.description: The job whose port the key follows. Two jobs may each declare a PORT — their environments are separate — so the port name alone does not identify a base. Required: every port belongs to exactly one job.

port.description: The port variable declared in a job's `ports` table, whose base is looked for inside the value.

port_probe_timeout.description: Seconds `wtm run up` waits for a declared port to answer before reporting it silent. Omit for the default (15); a negative value disables the check.

addressing.description: What an [[env_port]] link writes into a .env value: "ports" substitutes the port number wherever it sits in the value, "names" substitutes the whole origin for the links whose job publishes a name. Defaults to "names".

concurrency.description: What `wtm run up` does when another worktree already has jobs running: "parallel" leaves them alone, "exclusive" stops them first. Absent means the question has not been answered yet, and `run up` asks it once.
